  "name": "camels",

    {
      "id": "lay_fbrx6y",
      "type": "symbols",
      "name": "camels symbols",
      "comments": [
        { "id": "cmt_ignc6x", "address": "$0056", "placement": "after", "text": "Correction/addition: on the title-options screen (around $525E-$528D) this same location is toggled 0/1 with INC + AND #$01 to highlight a 1 PLAYER / 2 PLAYER choice, and is read as a plain zero/nonzero flag at $525E. So it holds 0/1 here but 1/2 once a game is running (sub_5359 etc compare it to 1 and 2). Either the menu writes 1/2 before starting the round, or there are two related-but-distinct uses of the same byte across game phases -- not confirmed which." },
        { "id": "cmt_tg6xbk", "address": "$0056", "text": "Zero page selector, seen compared against 1 and 2 (sub_539B, msg suffix patching) and against 2 alone (sub_5359, loc_561E). Chooses between player1_state/player2_state, and between the ONE/TWO suffix in msg_stand_by_player, msg_beasts_extinct and msg_enter_your_name. Zeroed once at cold start ($8A3C); where it is set to 1 or 2 has not been traced yet." }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "lay_ytakal",
      "type": "prg",
      "path": "revenge.d64:revenge fixed",
      "name": "packed"
    },
    {
      "id": "lay_ddlqxf",
      "type": "prg",
      "path": "runtime.prg",
      "name": "runtime",
      "comments": [
        { "id": "cmt_e53pa6", "address": "$0801", "text": "placeholder - will replace comment next" },
        { "id": "cmt_pdjwew", "address": "$0801", "text": "One large sprite sheet, ~288 standard 64-byte hi-res C64 sprites (24x21) back to back, from $0801 to $4FFF -- nothing in the code reached so far references it (no root existed before this claim; find_instructions on the VIC sprite-pointer range $07F8-$07FF and on STA $D000-$D010 turns up nothing yet, and it explicitly reports several indirect/computed-address writes it cannot resolve, so the code that actually points the VIC at a sprite number almost certainly lives in the still-undecoded $5E00-$87FD span). Visually (rendered in 16-wide grid chunks): recognisable camels in several walk/leg positions, small flying/aircraft-like enemies, falling parachute figures, devil/pitchfork and skeleton figures, a robot, the digits 0-9 and some letters, and a band roughly a third of the way through that renders as visual noise in this hi-res view -- possibly debris/explosion-particle sprites that are just genuinely busy-looking, possibly something not meant to be read as a plain hi-res sprite (multicolour mode, or a different frame boundary); not resolved. Could not tie any specific sprite index to a name (camel/enemy/digit-N) because the selecting code has not been found yet -- recorded only the visual grouping, not an index mapping." },
        { "id": "cmt_igjemn", "address": "$1D10", "text": "One byte per object slot (X, up to at least 16 slots -- sub_8B20 zeroes 16 of them at init). Holds the type/kind index of whatever occupies slot X, written by spawn_object_from_template ($9772) as TYA;STA dat_1D10,X right after copying that type's template fields. Read back all over the object-AI code ($9744,$97CB.. through $9C6B) as LDA/LDY dat_1D10,X to fetch Y = type, then Y indexes a further per-type table (e.g. dat_1DF8,Y) -- a two-level indirection: object slot -> type -> per-type property. This is the central \"one thing refers to another\" relation in the game logic." },
        { "id": "cmt_081em2", "address": "$1FB0", "text": "Per-object-slot byte (indexed by X, same slot numbering as obj_type at $1D10). Bit 7 is tested alone in several places (e.g. sub_9413: AND #$80) as an on/off flag; the low 7 bits, masked with AND #$7F, are doubled and used as the index into obj_behavior_jumptable ($9933) by sub_993A -- so this byte packs a flag and a behaviour selector together. Same AND #$7F / AND #$80 packing shows up on dat_1D60 and dat_1DF8 too -- a recurring one-flag-plus-7-bit-value convention across several of these per-object tables, not something the model here has a bitfield vocabulary for beyond this comment." },
        { "id": "cmt_zl1wt0", "address": "$5007", "text": "Copies 2048 bytes ($0800-$0FFF) from a source selected by bank_copy_ptr_tbl ($502F/$5030), indexed by X = zero page $02 as set by the caller before the JSR. Destination is fixed. Looks like a bank-switcher swapping some 2K asset (font or HUD graphics bank) into a shared work area; see the comment on bank_copy_ptr_tbl for why the exact table layout is not pinned down." },
        { "id": "cmt_l40dex", "address": "$502F", "text": "Read by sub_5007 (LDX from zp $02, then LDA dat_502F,X / LDA dat_5030,X to build a source pointer, then copies 2048 bytes to $0800-$0FFF). Only 1 byte of dat_502F and 11 of dat_5030 are visible in this gap; if read as (lo=dat_502F[X], hi=dat_5030[X]) with X stepping by 1, dat_5030 bytes 10,00,18,00,40,00,48,00,50,00,58 look like six little-endian 16-bit source addresses ($0010,$0018,$0040,$0048,$0050,$0058) rather than six separate lo/hi pairs looked up by a doubled index -- but this is read from the shape of the copy loop, not confirmed by seeing a caller set X, so treat the exact indexing scheme as unresolved." },
        { "id": "cmt_6ghxew", "address": "$511B", "text": "HUD line, decodes (screen-code) to a string ending in BEASTS REMAINING, one non-letter glyph byte, then a trailing 0. The trailing 0 is presumably overwritten at runtime with the live beast count." },
        { "id": "cmt_lpl6wz", "address": "$5199", "text": "HUD line, decodes to STAND BY YOUR BEAST, one non-letter glyph byte, then PLAYER ONE. That same glyph code is reused in msg_beasts_extinct and msg_enter_your_name below. The trailing ONE is patched to TWO for player 2 by suffix_two_patch_a, copied by sub_5143." },
        { "id": "cmt_r1y758", "address": "$51C0", "text": "Copied by sub_5143 (LDX#3; loop LDA suffix_two_patch_a,X / STA dat_05AE,X / DEX / BNE) over the tail of msg_stand_by_player's copy in the work buffer when zp location cur_player == 2. Only bytes 1-3 (TWO) are actually written; byte 0 (a space) is never copied since the loop stops at X==0." },
        { "id": "cmt_359vmc", "address": "$52C2", "text": "Section header on the title/options screen: OPTIONS" },
        { "id": "cmt_y4ohpy", "address": "$52C9", "text": "decodes to WAVE SEQUENCY then a non-letter glyph byte then NORMAL. Plotted unconditionally by sub_5216ish; the glyph is the same kind of decorative byte seen elsewhere (values above the A-Z/space/digit range)." },
        { "id": "cmt_c6tmtr", "address": "$52DE", "text": "decodes to PLAYERS then a glyph then 1. Only plotted (at $525B onward) when zero page $59 is set -- a second options row shown conditionally." },
        { "id": "cmt_5kd09f", "address": "$52E8", "text": "decodes to RANDOM. Companion label to opt_players_1, same conditional block." },
        { "id": "cmt_fxj7ge", "address": "$533F", "text": "decodes to DISTANCE BETWEEN ZONES then a glyph then 00. The trailing two-digit field is a BCD-ish counter at dat_05B0/dat_05B1, stepped by 2 (wrapping 0-20 back to 7) by sub_5300 when key scancode 6 (LSTX==6) is pressed on the options screen -- this is the difficulty/spacing setting, zero page $57 holds the raw value that dat_05B0/05B1 render as decimal." },
        { "id": "cmt_l6p131", "address": "$540C", "text": "HUD line, decodes to YOUR BEASTS ARE EXTINCT, the same non-letter glyph byte, then PLAYER ONE. Same ONE/TWO patch mechanism via suffix_two_patch_b." },
        { "id": "cmt_h8a5te", "address": "$5434", "text": "Same mechanism as suffix_two_patch_a at $51C0, duplicated here for sub_53EC's copy of msg_beasts_extinct instead of msg_stand_by_player." },
        { "id": "cmt_ija83h", "address": "$545C", "text": "Nothing calls this in the code reached so far, hence the missing root -- but it is unambiguous: LDX#0/LDA#$20/STA $5E00,X/INX/BNE fills all 256 bytes of $5E00-$5EFF with spaces, then LDA highscore_entry_1,X / AND #$3F / STA $5E00,X for X=0..207 copies the 208-byte default high-score table (highscore_entry_1..4 at $5474) into it, converting each byte from PETSCII/ASCII (the table encoding, letters 0x41-0x5A) to screen-code (0x01-0x1A) by masking the top two bits. This confirms, rather than just size-matches, that $5474 is the seed data for the $5E00 buffer the C0xx routines LOAD/SAVE as ATTACK MUTANT.HI." },
        { "id": "cmt_gigr1t", "address": "$5474", "text": "Default/shipped high-score table, 4 entries x 52 bytes = 208 bytes, the same size as the $5E00 buffer the C0xx routines LOAD/SAVE as ATTACK MUTANT.HI -- almost certainly the seed content for that file before any score is ever saved. Message: I LIKE CAMELS REALLY" },
        { "id": "cmt_ht3nt9", "address": "$54A8", "text": "Second slot of the default high-score table. Message: I GOT NOTHING AGAINST SHEEP EITHER" },
        { "id": "cmt_y76tc3", "address": "$54DC", "text": "Third slot of the default high-score table. Message: LLAMAS ARE LLOVELY" },
        { "id": "cmt_rxvz10", "address": "$5510", "text": "Fourth slot of the default high-score table. Message: 2D SPACE INVADERS RULE THE ZONE OK" },
        { "id": "cmt_c4lffs", "address": "$55ED", "text": "HUD line, decodes to ENTER YOUR NAME, the same glyph byte, then PLAYER, then ONE at offsets 24-26 and TWO at offsets 27-29 back to back. Unlike the two messages above, this one bakes both suffixes into the same table; the caller at loc_561E picks which 3-char window to read by adding 3 to the starting index when cur_player==2, instead of patching after the copy." },
        { "id": "cmt_qmohuo", "address": "$56AE", "text": "Values 0-1A (screen-code A-Z), then space, two more codes, then FF as a sentinel. Read by sub_5695 as kbd_char_table,X after X is found by scanning kbd_scan_table for the current LSTX value -- X is a shared index into both tables; this one gives the character to return." },
        { "id": "cmt_6afz88", "address": "$56CD", "text": "31 raw CIA keyboard scan codes (from LSTX / $C5), same length and same index space as kbd_char_table at $56AE. sub_5695 loops X 0..31 comparing LSTX against this table; a match at position X yields kbd_char_table[X] as the typed character. This is the keyboard-scancode-to-screen-code relation behind the name-entry screen (see msg_enter_your_name)." },
        { "id": "cmt_h6xyvh", "address": "$5756", "text": "decodes to HERE WE GO then three copies of the same non-letter glyph byte (0x51) then padding -- likely three exclamation-style decorative glyphs in this custom charset." },
        { "id": "cmt_v274be", "address": "$57A7", "text": "decodes to WELL DONE then a glyph then YOU HAVE SAVED CAMELKIND then the same glyph again then padding -- end-of-game congratulation message. The glyph (0x54) is yet another of the non-letter decorative bytes seen throughout this file (0x51/0x52/0x54/0x56 so far), consistent with punctuation drawn from a redefined character set rather than the standard A-Z range." },
        { "id": "cmt_nkcsoh", "address": "$57EF", "text": "decodes to CHEAT MODE OPERATIVE, space padded both sides." },
        { "id": "cmt_6twb5b", "address": "$5848", "text": "HUD line: PAUSE MODE ON, then space padding, then ANY KEY RESTARTS." },
        { "id": "cmt_6moprv", "address": "$5870", "placement": "after", "text": "Closer look: this repeats a small record shape roughly every 8-9 bytes -- a $00 terminator, two mystery bytes, a literal X, two more mystery bytes, a literal 6, a space, then a short mnemonic-shaped ASCII fragment (STA/RTS/TYA/PHA/AND/SEC/TAY/INY/LDA/ROL/DEY/BNE) with no operand. Reads like entries of the form (something, something, label-text) rather than raw code or a plain message. Not chased further -- would need to find what reads this table to know what the two mystery-byte fields are." },
        { "id": "cmt_dirw6d", "address": "$5870", "text": "Not understood. Read as plain ASCII/PETSCII it contains recognisable 6502-mnemonic-shaped fragments -- STA $07F7,X / RTS / TYA / PHA / AND #$07 / SEC / TAY / INY / LDA #$00 / ROL A / DEY / BNE -- interleaved with bytes outside printable range, so it is neither clean text nor anything this reading could place a shape on. Recorded as a plain data span rather than guessed at further; flagging this honestly instead of inventing a structure for it." },
        { "id": "cmt_s4kkfn", "address": "$5900", "text": "Two short tables of small paired bytes (roughly duration/value pairs), each ending in F0 FF 00 FF, then zero padding out to $5A00. Shape consistent with a short two-voice tune or sound-effect script (e.g. for the pause jingle heard nearby), but the exact field meaning was not traced into the SID-writing code that would confirm it." },
        { "id": "cmt_ce5ib0", "address": "$5A00", "text": "Long scrolling text block, ending exactly at $5E00 (the high-score save buffer). Opens WELCOME TO REVENGE OF THE MUTANT CAMELS / THIS PROGRAM WAS WRITTEN OVER A TWO MONTH PERIOD BY JEFF MINTER / THE INTRODUCTORY MUSIC WAS ARRANGED FOR TH[E...] and continues from there -- this confirms the game title and author from the bytes themselves. I already knew both facts about this real game before this reading; recording that here rather than presenting it as a bytes-only discovery. Not transcribed further by hand past the opening lines; 1024 bytes is a lot of scrolling prose and the point of this claim is coverage, not a full transcript." },
        { "id": "cmt_r8vuwu", "address": "$5E00", "text": "Live high-score slot 1 in the LOAD/SAVE buffer -- this is the one C0xx actually persists. Confirmed 52 bytes/entry, same layout as HighScoreEntry at $5474 but screen-code encoded (see seed_highscore_buffer at $545C)." },
        { "id": "cmt_dlr0ou", "address": "$5E34", "text": "Live high-score slot 2." },
        { "id": "cmt_qvnrxq", "address": "$5E68", "text": "Live high-score slot 3." },
        { "id": "cmt_yedzat", "address": "$5E9C", "text": "Live high-score slot 4." },
        { "id": "cmt_3r6h36", "address": "$5F00", "text": "Per-player save area, 128 bytes. Selected (alongside player2_state at $5F80) by cur_player in sub_5359/sub_539B, which swap it with the live screen row + zero page $58/$50/$54 so a split-screen two-player game can keep each side status separate. Seeded at cold start ($8A3C) from dat_90F8 for the first 40 bytes." },
        { "id": "cmt_pz34g2", "address": "$5F80", "text": "Same shape as player1_state at $5F00. First 40 bytes seeded at cold start ($8A3C) from the same source (dat_90F8) as player1_state; a separate 4-byte field at +8 (offset $5F88) is seeded from dat_8A38 by the loop right after." },
        { "id": "cmt_2fv58m", "address": "$5FFE", "text": "Pointer 13/14 is set to exactly 5FFE by sub_9170 before the sequencer at loc_88F7 runs. Verified (duration,note) pairs are plausible (duration under 20 hex, note in 20-45 hex or note=F0) up to offset 558 (622D); the next two bytes (80 F0) break that pattern and are followed by a run of 16 FF bytes -- likely a second tracks silence or header rather than more of this one, so extent stops there rather than guessing further. sub_9170 also sets a second pointer pair 15/16 = 631E, which read_bytes shows starting a similar-looking but not yet verified (duration,note) stream -- probably a second music track (title vs in-game vs game-over is a common multi-tune pattern for this kind of game) not yet fully bounded." },
        { "id": "cmt_1zpd10", "address": "$87FE", "text": "Builds a 40-entry (X 0..39) table of pointers to each screen row: dat_0340,X = low byte, dat_0360,X = high byte, starting at $0400 and adding $28 (40) each step -- the classic C64 screen-row-address lookup table, presumably to avoid recomputing row*40+col elsewhere." },
        { "id": "cmt_4o2k0x", "address": "$87FE", "text": "Already known as an entry point (called from loc_8A3C) but re-checking neighbourhood decode." },
        { "id": "cmt_t5mnhu", "address": "$8834", "text": "Forcing decode of a small undecoded gap between two already-decoded routines; bytes looked like plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_rvodbc", "address": "$883A", "text": "Writes A to screen via ($48),Y, then adds #$D4 to the pointer's high byte ($49) -- turning a screen-RAM pointer ($04xx-$07xx) into the matching Color-RAM pointer ($D8xx-$DBxx, since colour RAM = screen + $D400 -- $04+$D4=$D8) -- and writes a second byte (from $05) as the colour at the same offset. X (compared to #$28=40) looks like a column bound check. Called from many places (16 refs); the closest thing this program has to a print-character-with-colour primitive." },
        { "id": "cmt_lcoatq", "address": "$88D4", "text": "Forcing decode: undecoded span, checking whether it disassembles as plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_pohsmp", "address": "$88D4", "text": "Correction: this single RTI byte is separate from the real handler, which starts at $88D5 (raster_irq_handler_body) -- the disassembler stops at RTI so it does not fall through. edit_claim cannot revise a claim's comment or method, only name/is/extent/root, so this follow-up comment stands next to the original rather than replacing it." },
        { "id": "cmt_xq726k", "address": "$88D4", "text": "Raster IRQ handler (installed dynamically -- the reset path at $C0B9 sets the IRQ vector to the stock $EA31, so something later repoints it here). RTI as first byte is a stray leftover from an earlier RTI-terminated stub; the real body follows: LDA VICIRQ; AND #$01; BNE stock-IRQ($EA31); INC $1E (frame counter); JMP $8BC9 (main per-frame update, already claimed as a routine)." },
        { "id": "cmt_wd5323", "address": "$88D5", "text": "Separate from $88D4 (a bare RTI, one byte -- a stub/placeholder IRQ used before install, or the tail of alignment; the disassembler treats RTI as ending flow so this had to be rooted on its own). LDA VICIRQ; AND #$01; BNE stock-IRQ($EA31); INC $1E (frame counter); JMP $8BC9 (main per-frame update)." },
        { "id": "cmt_yw31w7", "address": "$88FE", "text": "Forcing decode of a small undecoded gap between two already-decoded routines; bytes looked like plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_ckvfr2", "address": "$898C", "text": "Low byte of a SID voice-1 frequency value, indexed by X = a note number read from a note/duration byte stream via LDA ($13),Y at $88F7 (loc_88F7 is a music sequencer: reads note at Y=0, duration/flag at Y=1 checked against terminator $F0, advances the 16-bit pointer $13/14 by 2 per step). Paired with sid_note_freq_hi at $89CD -- two parallel arrays (lo table, hi table) rather than one interleaved record, so add_type (which declares fields within one element) does not fit this shape; recording the pairing in these two comments/names is the workaround." },
        { "id": "cmt_d6139e", "address": "$89CD", "text": "High byte of the SID voice-1 frequency value for the same note index X as sid_note_freq_lo at $898C (STA V1FREQLO / STA V1FREQHI at $88F7). Values rise roughly exponentially ($02..$54), consistent with a chromatic-note frequency table." },
        { "id": "cmt_ciq1yi", "address": "$8A0E", "text": "Tail of the $898C-$8A3B span, right before loc_8A3C. No absolute-address reference found into this span. Bytes: 03 13 21 16 0F 09 25 1B 07 12 20 19 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 02 0B 06 07 08 03 04 06 07 09 03 08 05 0A 07 09 03 01 07 03 05 04 06 00 54 57 4F. Small values throughout, several short ascending runs (03 04 05 06 07 08 09 appears twice) -- guessing a further small table (durations? note-stream data reached only through the $13/14 pointer this project has not traced to an initial value?) but not confirmed. Last 3 bytes read as ASCII \"TWO\" -- possibly incidental, possibly the tail of a nearby string this claim's extent cut into; worth re-checking if $8A3C's neighbourhood changes." },
        { "id": "cmt_61z9x3", "address": "$8B5F", "text": "No absolute-address inbound reference found; forcing decode as a routine since the bytes disassemble cleanly as 6502 and dat_A000 (a jump table at $A000, see sub_8D1D) plausibly reaches it indirectly." },
        { "id": "cmt_cpmfni", "address": "$8B5F", "text": "X (masked to 0-7, then +1) selects a sprite. Stores zp $08 to dat_1F50+X and zp $07*2 to dat_1F40+X (shadow copies, not the real $D000 sprite registers -- probably built once per frame and blitted to hardware elsewhere so sprites do not tear mid-raster). Carry out of the ASL (i.e. bit 7 of the un-doubled value) sets or clears one bit of a 2-byte table at dat_1F9C, built via a shift-loop rather than a lookup -- the classic idiom for a sprite MSB/multicolour/priority register shadow, but I have not traced dat_1F9C to $D010 to confirm which VIC register it shadows." },
        { "id": "cmt_uzosqo", "address": "$8BAF", "text": "Immediately follows the RTS ending set_sprite_shadow_xy_and_msb; disassembles cleanly as 6502. Forcing decode -- likely reached the same way (indirectly / by a caller elsewhere not yet traced)." },
        { "id": "cmt_d9q8bv", "address": "$8BC9", "text": "Entered from the raster IRQ (raster_irq_handler_body, $88D5) on every raster interrupt. Dispatches on zp $1E (a phase counter, reset to 0 in the phase-3 arm below, otherwise not seen incremented in this routine -- the IRQ handler only does INC $1E before jumping here, so $1E cycles 0,1,2,0,1,2..): phase 1 sets the next raster split at $D8 and re-derives SCROLX from $1F; phase 2 sets the split at $F8, turns on the top of the display (clears SCROLY bit7) and rounds SCROLX down; the fallthrough (phase 0 / anything else) is the heavy one -- reads sprite-sprite collision (SPSPCL->$44), arms the next split at $90, calls sub_96D2 (a special-key check gate) and conditionally sub_508B, then runs a second, separate counter at $1F (0..7) that round-robins per-frame housekeeping: score/HUD countdowns at $2A/$29, a wrapping scroll counter at absolute dat_1F70 (not the per-object array of the same address -- a real address collision, not an alias), the wave animation trigger (JMP loc_9206) on count 4, and a table walk over dat_0630 on the rest. I decoded and covered all of this (no undecoded bytes remain in it) but did not chase every branch target to a name -- covered, not fully understood in the sense the brief means for the class of \"say what things are made of\"." },
        { "id": "cmt_h5bldk", "address": "$8BC9", "text": "Forcing decode: undecoded span, checking whether it disassembles as plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_mqcxqb", "address": "$8CA3", "text": "4 dead bytes: the JMP at $8CA0 lands at $8CA7, skipping these entirely. Forcing them to decode as code (BIT/EOR) produced an overlap warning against the real code at $8CA7 -- reverted. Bytes: 2C 3B 41 45." },
        { "id": "cmt_x419ue", "address": "$8CA3", "text": "Forcing decode of a small undecoded gap between two already-decoded routines; bytes looked like plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_pfdpzp", "address": "$8D25", "text": "Forcing decode: undecoded span, checking whether it disassembles as plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_0rbiaq", "address": "$8DF4", "text": "16 frames of 8 screen-codes each (indexed as frame*8+column by loc_8E74/loc_8E9A: X = frame_index*8, then 6 of the 8 bytes per frame are copied to dat_1FF0,Y, one column at a time). Screen codes $20 (blank) and $26-$2A (5 distinct glyphs) trace out a peak sliding left-right across the 8 columns and rising/falling through the 5 glyphs -- a wave/pulse animation, most likely the moving indicator I saw named NEUTRONIUM STATUS in hud_status_text ($90E4). Frame selection depends on zero-page $22/$23 (compared against #$03), not yet traced further." },
        { "id": "cmt_msj0ma", "address": "$8FCB", "text": "Forcing decode: undecoded span, checking whether it disassembles as plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_c5m46x", "address": "$90E4", "text": "Read via read_bytes, not disassembly -- an earlier attempt to force-decode this span as code produced garbage (SRE/illegal opcodes, JSRs to nonsense addresses). Full text: \"OF THE MUTANT CAMELS  PLAYER ONE  0000000  NEXT ZONE 00 KM    NEUTRONIUM STATUS  HHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH  \". The leading \"OF THE MUTANT CAMELS\" is the tail of the game title (REVENGE OF THE MUTANT CAMELS); the rest are score/status HUD field labels." },
        { "id": "cmt_hl0c5s", "address": "$90E4", "text": "Forcing decode: undecoded span, checking whether it disassembles as plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_kmoih8", "address": "$9149", "text": "Follows hud_status_text. 21 bytes of $01 then 07 07 07 04 04 04 repeated three times. Guess: a full/default neutronium status bar -- $01 as a bar-segment glyph, the 6-byte repeat as a colour or animation cycle for it -- not confirmed against the code that copies it to screen/colour RAM." },
        { "id": "cmt_2f9ern", "address": "$91BA", "text": "Forcing decode: undecoded span, checking whether it disassembles as plausible 6502." },
        { "id": "cmt_bkuwdd", "address": "$9259", "text": "6-entry symmetric ramp (0,1,2,3,2,1) read by LDA dat_9259,X in loc_9206 and stored to dat_2148,Y in a 16-iteration loop -- a triangle-wave index table, the same idiom as wave_anim_frames at $8DF4 but shorter and numeric rather than glyphs." },
